subject: Crescendo Labs - footprint & KV-cache forecast for Dedicated deployment
messages:
From: Evan Shaw <evan@crescendolab.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Narang <priya.narang@crescendolab.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated footprint ask - 70B / 32k context / KV-cache sizing

Kimberly / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re moving toward a reserved Dedicated deployment for our inference tier and need a concise footprint / GPU estimate to feed procurement and our infra team. Key points: 

- Model family: LlamaX-70B (we plan to pin to the 70B variant initially)
- Typical context: up to 32k tokens (mix of prompts + doc context) with heavy prefix reuse (many requests hit cached prefixes)
- Target SLO: P50 generation latency ~120ms for short completions (100-200 tokens), P95 best-effort
- Expected steady concurrency: 25–40 simultaneous active requests, peak bursts to ~80 for short windows
- Streaming: ~30% of calls will be streaming; remainder are standard sync generation

Questions we need answered for procurement: 1) model + KV-cache memory per GPU for common quantization profiles (FP16, 8-bit, 4-bit) 2) recommended GPU SKU(s) for Dedicated reserved pool 3) conservative committed GPU count to meet concurrency targets with 20% headroom 4) notes on latency impact of lower-precision quantization and on live KV-cache sizing/eviction behavior

We plan to start with a 12-month reserved commitment if numbers look sensible. Can you provide a short spreadsheet + a one-page summary we can attach to the procurement request?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement meeting is next Wednesday (June 14).

Best,
Evan Shaw
CTO, Crescendo Labs
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evan Shaw <evan@crescendolab.com>
Cc: Priya Narang <priya.narang@crescendolab.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated footprint ask - 70B / 32k context / KV-cache sizing

Evan — thanks for the clear ask. We’ll put together the spreadsheet and a short one-page summary for procurement. A few clarifying questions to make the numbers accurate: 

1) Concurrency profile: is 25–40 your steady-state concurrent active requests (requests that are generating tokens at the same time), or is that total sessions including idle reading stage?
2) Average response length: you said 100–200 tokens for short completions — is that the mode, or do you expect a long-tail to several thousand tokens for some workflows?
3) How important is strict P95 latency vs. P50? we can size aggressively for P95 but it increases committed GPU counts.

Prelim note: for 70B with 32k KV cache, the KV working set can be material (we typically see an additional ~0.6–0.8 bytes per token in the cache depending on architecture). We’ll include per-GPU footprint for FP16 / INT8 / 4-bit options and show recommended SKUs (A100-80, H100) with headroom multipliers. Attaching the draft model profiles and our estimate workbook — I’ll flag the cells with assumptions.

I’ll loop Marcus and Mina on the implementation-level tradeoffs and ask Marcus to drop a technical calc in thread. If acceptable, we can run a 2-hour sizing call tomorrow or Wednesday.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 8 Jun 2028 14:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated footprint ask - technical sizing notes

Kimberly / Mina / Evan — quick technical note with the back-of-envelope numbers I ran; I put the detailed calc into crescendo_memory_model_profiles.csv and referenced the workbook. High level: 

- Model memory (approx, excludes optimizer states and debug buffers):
  • 70B FP16 (activation + params meta): ~44 GB
  • 70B INT8 (score-corrected weight quant): ~30–32 GB (model-only footprint drops ~28–32%)
  • 70B 4-bit (QLoRA-style / nf4): ~20–22 GB (aggressive but workable with optimized kernels)

- KV-cache: for 32k context with typical kv-encoding we observe ~0.6–0.9 bytes/token in our runtime. That maps to roughly: 
  • 32k tokens -> ~19.2–28.8 MB per token count? (note: convert units below)
  • Practical summary: KV-cache add-on ranges ~18–26 GB depending on token encoding and whether you store prefix-only or full session history. We show per-GPU KV delta in the spreadsheet for both "full-session" and "prefix-only" policies.

- Recommended SKUs & placement:
  • A100-80GB: fits FP16 70B + KV-cache comfortably with around 10–15% headroom. Good price-performance for reserved pools.
  • H100-80GB: slightly better latency; better for mixed-precision kernels and upcoming int4 kernels. Higher unit cost.
  • With INT8 quant: a single A100-80 can host the model + KV for your steady short-concurrency use, but headroom reduces; we still recommend reserving at least 1 GPU worth of spare capacity per pool to handle bursts.

- Throughput sizing (target: P50 ~120ms, concurrency 25–40 steady): 
  • Conservative committed pool (FP16): 10 A100-80 GPUs (assumes batching and caching, 20% headroom).
  • With INT8: 7–8 A100-80 GPUs (same assumptions; remember INT8 improves memory but may slightly increase decode latency depending on kernel maturity).
  • With 4-bit aggressive quant and optimized kernels: 5–6 GPUs possible but higher variance — recommend this only after an evaluation run.

- Latency tradeoffs: INT8 generally reduces memory and can improve cache locality but may add 3–15ms of decode overhead depending on kernel paths and attention optimizations; 4-bit can add additional CPU/GPU packing overhead. We’ve captured per-path estimates in the workbook.

- Operational notes: 
  • KV eviction: prefer prefix-only retention for doc-heavy workloads to keep steady KV working set small; full-session retention multiplies KV usage substantially.
  • Autoscaling: reserve the committed pool for baseline; enable burst pools that can spin up cheaper spot instances for rare spikes. Discussed in the estimate workbook.

I’ll be available on the sizing call to walk through the spreadsheet and the assumptions.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Marcus — this is extremely helpful, thanks. A couple quick follow-ups: 

- We are comfortable starting committed pool sizing on the INT8 plan (tradeoffs acceptable) — can you confirm the 7–8 A100-80 number is for steady-state 25–40 concurrency with 20% headroom, correct?
- For procurement we need a one-line description of risk if the vendor (GPU cloud) changes instance availability mid-contract — do you have recommended fallback model variants (e.g., move to 4-bit smaller model like 30B with different routing) that we can include?

If you can confirm the numbers and drop a 1-paragraph procurement note we’ll attach to the purchase order and aim to sign the commitment next week. Also please share the workbook cells you referenced so we can include them in the deck.

Thanks — Evan
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated footprint ask - 70B / 32k context / KV-cache sizing

Evan — confirmed. The 7–8 A100-80 GPUs is our recommended committed pool for INT8 with the concurrency and 20% headroom assumptions you listed. Attached is the dedicated_estimate_v2.xlsx with the highlighted cells and a one-paragraph procurement note you can paste into your PO: 

"Procurement note: Redwood Inference recommends a 12-month committed Dedicated pool of 7–8 A100-80 GPUs (INT8 quantized LlamaX-70B) to meet steady-state concurrency of 25–40 with 20% headroom and a P50 latency objective near 120ms. In the event of constrained instance availability, Redwood recommends an automated routing policy to fall back to either (a) a compatible INT8 H100 pool or (b) a policy-driven model variant downgrade to LlamaX-30B (4-bit) for non-critical workloads while maintaining core SLAs. Pricing and final GPU counts to be confirmed post-validation run.

I’ll schedule a 30-minute validation/hand-off session with Marcus and Mina tomorrow afternoon to walk procurement and infra through the highlighted workbook cells.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: dedicated_estimate_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), crescendo_memory_model_profiles.csv (model calc)
"
